extracted.intended_audience: researchers and authors in mathematical physics (potential submitters and readers)
extracted.subtask_short: submitting to Communications in Mathematical Physics
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and high-level information for authors/readers about the scope, standards, and journal-level metrics for Communications in Mathematical Physics, a Springer journal publishing original research in mathematical physics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mission / scope and quality
rubrics_metrics.description: The mission of Communications in Mathematical Physics is to offer a high forum for works which are motivated by the vision and the challenges of modern physics and which at the same time meet the highest mathematical standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submissions should be motivated by modern-physics problems or perspectives and must satisfy very strong mathematical rigor/standards. This is the primary editorial scope criterion for acceptability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Article type: OriginalPaper
rubrics_metrics.description: Articles listed on the page are labeled 'OriginalPaper'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The journal publishes original research papers (OriginalPaper). Authors should prepare manuscripts as original contributions suitable for this article type; other article types (reviews, letters, etc.) are not shown on this page.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special issues / collections policy (invitation-only noted)
rubrics_metrics.description: Part of 1 collection: Special issue dedicated to the memory of Huzihiro Araki (submission by invitation only).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some special issues or collections exist and may restrict submissions to invited contributions only. Authors cannot assume open submission to such themed collections unless explicitly invited.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open access availability
rubrics_metrics.description: This journal has 1054 open access articles; individual article listings show 'Open access'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The journal supports open-access articles (some or many articles are OA). The page does not give the specific APC/policy details, but authors should expect an open-access option or hybrid model and consult full policy pages for requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Journal impact metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: Journal Impact Factor 2.6 (2024); 5-year Journal Impact Factor 2.7 (2024).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These metrics indicate the journal's citation-based impact and may be used by authors and institutions to assess venue prestige; they are descriptive rather than acceptance criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial turnaround time (median)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides an expected median time from submission to first editorial decision; useful for authors who need a sense of review speed. Actual times may vary by manuscript and year.

rubrics_metrics.name: Usage / readership metric (downloads)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A global usage metric showing cumulative downloads; indicative of readership/exposure but not a submission or quality requirement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abstracting and indexing coverage
rubrics_metrics.description: Abstracted and indexed in: ANVUR; Astrophysics Data System (ADS); BFI List; Baidu; CLOCKSS; CNKI; CNPIEC; Chinese Academy of Medical Science (CAMS); Current Contents/Physical, Chemical and Earth Sciences; Dimensions; EBSCO; Google Scholar; INSPEC; INSPIRE; Japanese Science and Technology Agency (JST); Mathematical Reviews; Naver; Norwegian Register for Scientific Journals and Series; OCLC WorldCat Discovery Service; Ovid Discovery; Portico; ProQuest; SCImago; SCOPUS; Science Citation Index Expanded (SCIE); TD Net Discovery Service; Wanfang; eLibrary.ru; zbMATH.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The journal is widely indexed, which affects discoverability and institutional recognition. Authors should consider indexing coverage when evaluating the journal's visibility for their work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication identifiers (ISSN)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standard bibliographic identifiers for citation and library cataloguing; not submission criteria but relevant for formatting and metadata.
